evidence.excerpt: Dana Incorporated, 2026: the board appointed Byron Foster Chief Executive Officer effective 1 July 2026; R. Bruce McDonald, Chairman and CEO since 2024, continues as Chairman of the Board. Foster joined Dana in 2021 to lead the company's global commercial, marketing and communications efforts and latterly served as Senior Vice President and President of Light Vehicle Systems, Dana's largest business unit. Earlier roles: VP & General Manager at Johnson Controls (2012-2016), EVP at Adient (2016-2019), CEO of Shield T3 (2020-2021); director of Wabtec. BBA University of Michigan, MBA Northwestern.

Dana Incorporated / Eaton, 11 June 2026: definitive agreement under which Eaton will separate its Mobility Group (Vehicle and eMobility segments) and combine it with Dana in a Reverse Morris Trust, creating a combined company valued at more than $10 billion. The transaction values Eaton's Mobility Group at approximately $5.1 billion. The combined company is expected to have approximately $11 billion in sales and approximately $1.7 billion adjusted EBITDA on a fully synergised pro forma 2026 estimated basis, with $250 million of run-rate synergies within 24 months of closing. Eaton receives a cash distribution of approximately $1.1 billion; Eaton shareholders will own at least 50.1 per cent of the combined company. Closing expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to Dana shareholder approval and regulatory clearances. Also carried by PRNewswire (302797498), Eaton's newsroom and Dana's Form 8-K / Form 425.

Dana Incorporated full-year 2025 results: sales of $7.5 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $610 million (8.1 per cent margin) and net income of $85 million, against a net loss of $57 million a year earlier. Sales fell year on year because Dana divested its Off-Highway business to focus on light- and commercial-vehicle markets.

Dana TM4 is a joint venture between Dana Incorporated and Hydro-Quebec. TM4 Inc., a Hydro-Quebec subsidiary, became Dana's source for electric motors, power inverters and control systems, with Dana taking a majority shareholding in exchange for about $127 million (2018).

Dana Incorporated: a 4,600 square-metre facility in Pune, India producing Dana TM4 low- to high-voltage electric motors, inverters and vehicle control units - Dana's eighteenth facility in India. Pune is one of India's leading automotive hubs and home to OEMs including Bajaj Auto, Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra.

Dana Incorporated is based in Maumee, Ohio. Timothy R. Kraus was appointed senior vice president and chief financial officer in December 2021, having previously been senior vice president of finance and treasurer; earlier roles at Intelsat, Lear Corporation and Ernst & Young. R. Bruce McDonald is Chairman of the Board. No chief marketing officer is named on Dana's leadership listing.

Formula E sponsor table: Mahindra Racing - Mahindra & Mahindra (title) and Tech Mahindra; no driveline, e-propulsion, thermal or components partner. DS Penske - Mouser Electronics, TTI Inc., Molex, KYOCERA AVX, TotalEnergies. Jaguar TCS Racing - TCS (title), Castrol, Jaguar powertrain. Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team - Lola Cars, Yamaha, ABT Sportsline, Castore, OMP, Shell. Envision Racing - Envision Group, Sand Technologies, Teijin, Genpact. Andretti Formula E - Andretti Global, TWG AI, Quest Global, Crowe UK, Reflo, Nissan powertrain. Porsche Formula E Team - Porsche, TAG Heuer, Hugo Boss. Nissan Formula E Team - Nissan, Coral, Crowe, Nagase, Castrol. Cupra Kiro - Cupra, Kiro. Citroen Racing - Citroen, Stellantis. Series level: ABB, DHL, Julius Baer, Hankook, Google Cloud, Saudia, PIF, Infosys, TAG Heuer, SXSW.

Formula E calendar table: the London E-Prix closes the 2025-26 season at ExCeL on 15-16 August 2026; the GEN4 era begins with the 2026-27 season. Formula E lists Jaguar, Nissan, Citroen, Lola Cars, Mahindra and Porsche among the manufacturers committed to GEN4.

brief.deck: Dana Incorporated, the $7.5 billion driveline and e-propulsion supplier, agreed on 11 June to combine with Eaton's Mobility Group in a Reverse Morris Trust - an $11 billion-sales vehicle-systems company closing in the first quarter of 2027, under a new chief executive who came up through commercial and marketing.
brief.the_case_p1: Eaton and Dana signed a definitive agreement on 11 June 2026 to separate Eaton's Mobility Group and combine it with Dana in a Reverse Morris Trust, creating a company valued at more than $10 billion. The transaction values Mobility at about $5.1 billion and the combined business at roughly $11 billion of sales and $1.7 billion of adjusted EBITDA on a fully synergised pro forma 2026 basis, with $250 million of run-rate synergies inside 24 months. Eaton shareholders take at least 50.1 per cent. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027.
brief.the_case_p2: Dana closed 2025 with $7.5 billion of sales, $610 million of adjusted EBITDA and $85 million of net income after divesting Off-Highway, a supplier that has already chosen its ground in light and commercial vehicles. Byron Foster became chief executive on 1 July 2026. He joined Dana in 2021 to run global commercial, marketing and communications, so brand investment is his own discipline rather than a delegated one.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The combination closes in the first quarter of 2027 and the new company puts its name into the market then. Formula E's GEN4 era begins the same season, and teams settle their partner tables through the autumn.
brief.why_team_para: Mahindra Racing carries only Mahindra & Mahindra and Tech Mahindra on its partner table, so the driveline, e-propulsion and thermal lane sits open at a works team committed to the GEN4 era. Dana's India footprint is real: eighteen facilities, and a Pune plant building Dana TM4 electric motors, inverters and vehicle control units in the city Mahindra & Mahindra calls home. The commercial conversation starts before the sponsorship one.
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Dana TM4 builds electric motors, power inverters and control systems; Dana engineers thermal management, sealing and driveline for light and commercial vehicles. That gives a works team's powertrain group a real supplier bench to work against, with Mahindra's road-car programme behind it. In return Dana gets a named technical partnership, livery presence, and a paddock of manufacturers that is its own customer base.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Driveline & e-Propulsion Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, so the term opens with the combined company's first year and the GEN4 era together. Estimated $1.5-3M a year, part-payable in engineering support. Scope: sidepod and halo placement, an engineering programme with the powertrain group, and hospitality at the European and Asian rounds.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Foster became CEO on 1 July 2026 after leading Dana's global commercial, marketing and communications from 2021 and running Light Vehicle Systems, its largest unit. Path: R. Bruce McDonald, Chairman, and Timothy Kraus, CFO since December 2021. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the new company, not the old one.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Byron, you spent five years selling Dana before you ran it. In early 2027 you launch a company with $11 billion of sales that needs a name buyers know, and Formula E's paddock is your customer list. 25 minutes?”
score_cells: Agreement signed 11 Jun; the company itself lands Q1 2027.
Tier-1 supplier; no consumer pull, but the paddock buys.
No hard deadline beyond the Season 13 roster window.
MODE A: e-motors, inverters, thermal and driveline bench.
risks: The combined business does not exist until the Reverse Morris Trust closes, expected in the first quarter of 2027 and subject to Dana shareholder approval.
Contract now on a term starting at close, so the brand launch and Season 13 land together.
A SUPPLIER, NOT A CONSUMER BRAND
Dana sells to vehicle makers, so a livery has no retail job to do and the board will ask what it buys.
Price it as customer marketing against a trade budget: the paddock is manufacturers, not shoppers.
brief.bottom_line: A vehicle-systems company with about $11 billion of sales is being assembled in public, and the executive who ran Dana's commercial and marketing function now runs the company. Mahindra Racing's partner table is nearly bare, Dana builds e-propulsion in Pune, and the GEN4 era begins as the deal closes.

why_team.label: The audience is the customer list
why_team.text: The Formula E paddock is Jaguar, Nissan, Citroen, Lola Cars, Mahindra and Porsche. For a company that sells electrified propulsion to vehicle makers, that is a season-long trade show with its buyers already in the room.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Dana TM4 builds electric motors, power inverters and control systems; Dana engineers thermal management, sealing and driveline hardware. A works team's powertrain group gets a supplier bench to test ideas against between seasons, and Dana gets an engineering reference it can show to every other manufacturer on the grid.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: Mahindra Racing gains a partner whose customers are vehicle makers and fleet operators, which widens the guest list at the European and Asian rounds beyond the team's Indian corporate base and gives the commercial team a category it can sell again.

value.label: Talent and content
value.text: Electrification engineering recruitment is the hardest hiring market Dana has; a Formula E programme is the recruitment story that works with graduate engineers. On the content side, road-car transfer from a works Formula E programme is a narrative both parties can film.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Driveline & e-Propulsion Partner designation, sidepod and halo placement, an engineering exchange with the powertrain group, hospitality at the European and Asian rounds, and driver access for Dana's customer and recruitment channels.

ruled_out.reason: Mouser Electronics, TTI Inc., Molex and KYOCERA AVX already fill the components and electronics lane, with TotalEnergies on energy.
Castrol holds the fluids and driveline-adjacent lane, and Jaguar's own powertrain programme sits above any Tier-1 partnership.
A manufacturer team with its own powertrain supply chain; TAG Heuer and Hugo Boss hold the visible partner slots.
Nissan supplies its GEN4 powertrain to a customer team as well as itself, so a rival Tier-1 on the car sits inside its own supply politics; Castrol and Nagase already on the roster.
Sand Technologies, Teijin and Genpact occupy the technology and materials lanes, and Envision Group's own energy business dominates the brand story.
TWG AI, Quest Global, Crowe UK and Reflo occupy the engineering-services and technology lanes; Nissan supplies the powertrain.

ruled_out.team: Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team
ruled_out.reason: Yamaha's powertrain and Shell's energy partnership crowd the technical lane, and Lola's constructor identity owns the engineering story.
Both have room, but neither carries a commercial adjacency to Dana's customer base of the kind Pune gives Mahindra.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Byron Foster before the autumn roster round to size an Official Driveline & e-Propulsion Partner entry at Mahindra Racing on a three-year term starting at the close of the Eaton transaction, and to agree who from Light Vehicle Systems joins the engineering conversation.

## Screen-outs and things deliberately not claimed

- **Leadership ties: none found.** No Formula E or Formula 1 history was found for Byron Foster,
  R. Bruce McDonald or Timothy Kraus after checking. `leadership_ties` is empty, not assumed.
- **No claim that Dana supplies Mahindra.** The verified adjacency is geographic and industrial:
  Dana's Pune e-drive plant sits in the city Mahindra & Mahindra is headquartered in. A supply
  relationship was not found and is not asserted.
- **No Dana motorsport heritage claim.** The Spicer driveline brand has a racing history in
  general circulation, but no primary source was opened for it in this session, so the brief does
  not use it.
- **Deal size ($1.5-3M a year) is an ESTIMATE**, labelled as such, and set at Formula E team
  rates rather than Formula 1 ones.
- **The pro forma $11B / $1.7B figures are the parties' own projection**, not reported results;
  the brief says "pro forma" every time they appear.

## Why not the other teams

Judged only against `seeds/sponsors.json`, never against other 1440 prospects. Every conflicting
team is named in `extended.ruled_out` with the partner that closes the lane.

## Honest brake on the score

74/100. Timing is the weak dimension: the agreement is signed but the company itself does not
exist until Q1 2027, so this is a relationship to open now and sign at close, not a deal to
announce in the next month. Brand fit is 13 because Dana sells to vehicle makers and a livery
has no retail work to do — the case for it is customer marketing, and the brief says so.
